name: Jehozadak
title: The High Priest Taken into Exile
summary: Jehozadak (also known as Josedek) was the son of the high priest Seraiah and the father of the high priest Joshua (Jeshua), who led the rebuilding of the temple after the exile. Jehozadak was taken into captivity when Nebuchadnezzar conquered Jerusalem and destroyed the temple in 586 BC. His significance lies primarily in his role as a link in the high priestly lineage between the first and second temples.

keyEvents.title: Jehozadak's Place in the Line of High Priests
keyEvents.description: Jehozadak is mentioned as the son of Seraiah in the high priestly lineage that traces back to Aaron through Zadok. This line documents the legitimate priestly succession.

keyEvents.title: The Exile to Babylon
keyEvents.description: Jehozadak was taken away when the Lord allowed Judah and Jerusalem to be carried off by Nebuchadnezzar. This marked the interruption of the high priestly service in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Father of the high priest Joshua
keyEvents.description: Jehozadak is known as the father of Joshua (Jeshua), who became high priest after returning from Babylon and led the rebuilding of the altar and temple together with Zerubbabel.

keyEvents.title: Joshua's appointment mentioned by the prophet Haggai
keyEvents.description: The prophet Haggai refers to Joshua, son of Jehozadak, as high priest, and urges him along with Zerubbabel to rebuild the Lord's temple.

keyEvents.title: Jehozadak's son in the prophet Zechariah's vision
keyEvents.description: The prophet Zechariah receives a vision where the high priest Joshua, son of Jehozadak, stands before the angel of the Lord and is cleansed from guilt, symbolizing the people's restoration.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in Ezra's genealogy
keyEvents.description: In the book of Ezra, Jehozadak's lineage is mentioned in connection with those who returned from exile and the rebuilding of the temple in Jerusalem.
